Its cost claim: I re-measured the nested rich_text chains I built in round 3 and the reviewer's own worst shape. proof.observed: The cost is linear now. One chain: 500 levels 0.0088 s, 1,000 0.0125 s, 2,000 0.0240 s, 4,000 0.0509 s, 4,990 0.0970 s, against 0.063/0.222/0.855/3.872/6.014 s at round 3 — a 62-fold drop at the deepest the elements-array shape reaches. The reviewer's worst shape, four chains 9,900 deep chained through a plain object key, body 990,398 B inside the 1 MiB cap: 0.2265 s, against the 85.4 s it measured in process at round 3. Two shapes of my own that would have caught a remaining re-measure path: an alternating section/rich_text chain 4,900 deep, 0.0931 s, and 2,000 sibling rich_text blocks, 0.0228 s. The round 3 listener answers that alternating body with `curl: (52) Empty reply from server`, its write timeout cutting the connection, where this head answers 200 in a tenth of a second.
proof.negativeControl: The same bodies with `text` empty, where the measurement never runs: 4,990 levels 0.0475 s here and 0.0497 s at round 3, so the drop is the measurement's and not the parser's; and a blocks tree nested 60,000 deep is still refused HTTP 400 by the JSON decoder with the listener still serving the next post.

risksForTheArchitect: R1 — the approved spec and the shipped code now differ in five named ways, each of them your ruling and none of them a defect I found: the walk knows `rich_text` by name, where version 11 says it 'never has to know the kind of a block or an attachment' and that 'the one exception is a deleted message'; it reads nine display names, where version 11 names seven; it reads blocks before attachments, where version 11 writes 'its `attachments` and `blocks`'; an attachment's field arrives as the synthesised line `title: value`, a string the message does not hold anywhere, where version 11 says the pieces are 'the strings under the field names'; and each line of the message's own text counts as already delivered, where version 11 compares the own text whole. The CHANGELOG and the controller reference describe the code correctly, so what a reader of this repository meets is right; it is the approved document that no longer says what ships. Whether that needs a new version is yours, and a new version closes the gate.

rounds.summary: Passed with three risks recorded: the containment repeat rule, the unproven 'reads as it did' claim for a literal & < >, and the alphabetical order inside one object. Review round 1 drove all three as findings and the architect withdrew its containment ruling.

Failed on one defect: the rich_text exception dropped an app's own rich text, not only the Slack client's copy. Pinned by the red test `an app's rich-text words beside a short text of its own`, committed at 0a049686c832 and unmodified since. Review round 1's three findings were verified fixed in the same round.

Passed: the round 2 failure was fixed and the red test went green. One measured risk was recorded rather than failed — the narrowing re-asked its own-words question at every nested rich_text object, 6.014 s at 4,990 levels against 0.058 s at round 2 — with the reachability unproven. Review round 2 measured the real bound (85.4 s inside the 1 MiB cap, past the listener's 10 s write timeout), the architect required the fix, and round 4 carries it.
